variants.headline: We fall to last place among the powers
body: The latest count of national scores places us last among {{count}} major powers. We did not hold this position at the previous count.

variants.headline: Last place, and the reckoning behind it
body: Our nation now trails every scored major power, {{count}} in all. The score is a ledger of choices: what we built, what we kept and what we defended.
The record shows where we stand. What it cannot show is who intends to answer for it.

variants.headline: Citizens, we are last!
body: Last of {{count}} powers, and the council tells us the tally is complicated. Bread is not complicated. Wages are not complicated.
This paper asks one question: who in the palace owns this result?

variants.headline: Last of {{count}} in the national scores
body: The standings are out. We're last of {{count}}. On the bright side, there's only one direction left to go.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} enters a golden age
body: A golden age has begun in {{civilization}}, a period of national flourishing. Such ages lift the fortunes of the state that enjoys them.

variants.headline: Notice from abroad: a golden age in {{civilization}}
body: We are informed that {{civilization}} has entered a golden age. Letters from its capital speak of flourishing affairs and a confident court.

variants.headline: A rival flourishes, and the balance shifts
body: {{civilization}} has begun a golden age, and a flourishing rival is a stronger rival. Prosperity pays for armies as surely as for festivals.
Its strength will count for more in every negotiation that follows. Ours should count for no less.

variants.headline: The neighbor's granary is full
body: When the neighbor's granary fills, the wise count their own grain.

variants.headline: The golden age of {{civilization}} ends
body: The golden age of {{civilization}} has run its course. The period of national flourishing is over, and ordinary times resume.

variants.headline: An age ends in {{civilization}}
body: At its height, the golden age of {{civilization}} filled its markets and lent its court a confident air. Like all such ages, it was granted, not owned.
It has now been taken back. What remains is for {{civilization}} to prove what it keeps without it.

variants.headline: The record of {{civilization}}: the age is done
body: In this season the golden age of {{civilization}} came to its end, as such ages have always ended. The court continues. The flourish is spent.

variants.headline: A golden age begins at home
body: Our nation has entered a golden age, with the country at peace. The government can expect a period of unusual flourishing.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age is upon us
body: Hear it, people! A golden age has begun for our nation, and we are at peace. A golden age, and peace with it! Let the news run through the streets.

variants.headline: The golden age, earned
body: A golden age does not begin by accident. It follows years of steady government, sound accounts and kept peace, and the nation now enjoys the return.
This paper's view: the age should be spent wisely, and the credit shared with those who earned it.

variants.headline: Sir, they call it golden
body: Sir, the capital has declared a golden age, and I am told the court is delighted. In my street the flour costs the same as it did on Monday.
I ask only: when does golden reach the bakers?

variants.headline: The morning the age turned golden
body: In the market they were already saying it by noon: good times have come, and no war to spoil them. One fruit seller gave away the bruised apples for the joy of it.
Golden age or not, free apples are free apples.

variants.headline: Our golden age ends
body: The golden age of our nation has come to its end. The period of flourishing is over, and ordinary times resume.

variants.headline: The age we had
body: It was a good age. Markets were full, the mood was generous, and the nation spoke of itself with pride. Such ages have always been borrowed rather than owned.
The loan is called in. What we built in the good years is what we keep.

variants.headline: After the golden age, the next one
body: The golden age is over, and the error would be to mourn it rather than to start earning the next.
Prosperity was built once. The same work, begun again, builds it twice.

variants.headline: A golden age begins, even against {{enemies}}
body: Our nation has entered a golden age while at war with {{enemies}}. The period of flourishing begins with the fighting unfinished.

variants.headline: A golden age begins in wartime
body: Our nation has entered a golden age even as the war goes on. Flourishing at home, fighting abroad: the two will now share the same years.

variants.headline: Golden, and still at war
body: A golden age has begun with our soldiers still in the field. That is luck, and luck is not a plan.
This paper's view: spend the age on the war while the war lasts, and let the peace find us prepared rather than spent.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age, even in war!
body: Hear it, people! A golden age is ours while we fight {{enemies}}! Let them hear it too: we flourish while we fight!

variants.headline: National happiness rises past half
body: National happiness has climbed to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, past the halfway mark. The contented now outnumber the discontented.

variants.headline: The national mood has mended
body: Good news at home tonight. National happiness now stands at {{happinessPercentage}} percent. The government's course holds, and the numbers show it.

variants.headline: Back above half, and it shows
body: The number is {{happinessPercentage}} percent, but you could read it on the trams: fewer arguments, longer queues at the cake shop, a busker playing something cheerful.
Half the country's mood is arithmetic. The other half is cake.

variants.headline: Citizens: the hard days have eased
body: The tally says {{happinessPercentage}} percent of us are content, and the tally has not said that in a while. Enjoy it. And remember who stewarded the lean years.

variants.headline: Our nation takes up {{ideology}}
body: The government has adopted the ideology of {{ideology}}, the first guiding doctrine the state has taken. The decision sets the direction of national politics from here.

variants.headline: A doctrine for the state
body: The state has chosen {{ideology}}, and a chosen doctrine is a public promise about what the government will value.
Allies and rivals will now read our politics by it. The question for the years ahead is whether the promise is kept.

variants.headline: A doctrine descends from the capital
body: The palace has adopted {{ideology}}, and no one below the palace was asked. Doctrine is easy at the top, where it costs nothing.
This paper asks: what does {{ideology}} do for the man at the plough? Answer that first.

variants.headline: The state takes a doctrine
body: We are informed that the government has adopted {{ideology}} as its guiding ideology. The old ways of governing served earlier generations well; time will tell how the new doctrine serves us.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} abandons {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}
body: The government of {{civilization}} has set aside {{formerIdeology}} and taken up {{ideology}}. The change of doctrine remakes its politics at a stroke.

variants.headline: A major power changes its ideology
body: One of the world's major powers has changed its guiding ideology, setting aside {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}. Its name has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: Our government changes doctrine
body: Our state has set aside {{formerIdeology}} and taken up {{ideology}}. The direction of national politics changes with it, at home and before the world.

variants.headline: A change of doctrine recorded
body: In this season the government of {{civilization}} set aside {{formerIdeology}} and took up {{ideology}}. The court remains; the doctrine does not.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} is reduced to a single city
body: The nation of {{civilization}}, once counted among the major powers, now holds one city. It held more than one until recently.

variants.headline: A major power reduced to one city
body: One of the world's major powers now holds a single city, having held more until recently. Its name has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: The remaining holdings of {{civilization}}
body: Cities now held: 1
Cities lost in recent turns: {{lost}}
A major power, at its last walls.

variants.headline: The wide lands of {{civilization}}
body: They say the roads of {{civilization}} once ran between many cities. Now the roads are quiet, and one city keeps the name.
An old trader put it plainly: a house with one room still stands, but it is not the house it was.

variants.headline: The government adopts {{policy}}
body: Our government has adopted the policy of {{policy}}, the newest measure in its program of state. Its effects begin now.

variants.headline: Notice of a new policy
body: We are informed that the government has adopted {{policy}}. The measure takes its place in the state's program, and ministers expect it to serve the nation well.

variants.headline: {{policy}}: a wager on what works
body: A policy is a hypothesis: the state acts, and the record will show whether the action helped.
The government has adopted {{policy}}. The measurable question is simple. What improves, and by how much?

variants.headline: New policy, old question
body: The government has adopted {{policy}}, and the announcement is splendid as always. Splendid announcements do not fill bowls.
This paper wants one number with the policy: what changes at the kitchen table? Publish it, then celebrate.

variants.headline: The state opens a new branch of policy
body: Our government has opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, bringing the state's pursuits to {{count}} in all. The new direction begins now.

variants.headline: New branches of policy open at once
body: Our government has opened more than one new branch of policy in a single stroke. The state now pursues {{count}} branches in all.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{branch}} branch is open
body: Hear it, people! Your government has opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, {{count}} branches now in hand! Good governance, and more of it!

variants.headline: The {{branch}} branch, recorded
body: In this season the court opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, and the state's pursuits now number {{count}}. Set down as it happened, for the record.

variants.headline: The threat of revolt recedes
body: National happiness has risen to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, above the level at which revolt threatens. The nation remains short of the halfway mark, where the contented outnumber the discontented.

variants.headline: Out of the danger zone, not yet safe
body: The national mood has climbed to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, past the level where revolt threatens. Recovery, on this record, has a direction, and it is the government's course.
Half is where contentment properly begins. The distance left is the work left.

variants.headline: Happiness update: out of revolt range
body: National happiness: {{happinessPercentage}} percent. That's above the revolt threshold for the first time in a while. Still below half, though. Not out of the woods.

variants.headline: National happiness falls below the revolt threshold
body: National happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, below the level at which revolt threatens. The discontented now outnumber the contented by a wide margin.

variants.headline: Hear it! The people are angry!
body: Hear it, hear it! The nation's happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, past the line where revolt threatens! Bread, work and peace of mind: the people want them back!

variants.headline: Below the line, and who is counting
body: National happiness stands at {{happiness}} percent, past the threshold where revolt threatens. This did not fall on the government from the sky.
This paper's demand: name the causes, and name who will carry the remedy. The street is already counting.

variants.headline: Happiness falls past revolt threshold
body: This is the national bulletin. Happiness now stands at {{happiness}} percent. That is below the revolt threshold. Repeat: below the threshold. The nation's mood is a matter of state.

variants.headline: {{name}} takes up {{ideology}}
body: The nation of {{name}} has adopted the ideology of {{ideology}}. Its politics now answer to a doctrine, where before they had none.

variants.headline: A rival power takes up {{ideology}}
body: One of the world's major powers has adopted the ideology of {{ideology}}, its first guiding doctrine. Its name has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: {{name}} now shares our doctrine
body: We are informed that {{name}} has embraced {{ideology}}, the same doctrine that guides our own state. Common convictions make easier neighbors, and we welcome the company.

variants.headline: {{name}} has a doctrine now
body: {{name}} has adopted {{ideology}}. A nation with a doctrine is a nation with a direction, and directions can be aimed.
Watch what it builds next. Doctrine tells you the target before any declaration does.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} takes first place among the powers
body: The latest reckoning of national scores places {{civilization}} first among the major powers. Another power held the lead before.

variants.headline: A new power leads the reckoning
body: The latest reckoning of national scores has a new leader among the major powers. The name behind the change has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: First place in score: {{civilization}}
The lead: shared with another major power
One first place, two claimants

variants.headline: Our nation stands first
body: The reckoning of national scores now places us first among the major powers. First place is a fact; keeping it is a program.
The next reckoning is already worth preparing for.

variants.headline: National happiness falls below half
body: National happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, a drop of {{drop}} points from the last reckoning. The discontented now outnumber the contented.

variants.headline: Below half, and falling
body: The national mood has dropped {{drop}} points to {{happiness}} percent, below half. Ministers call the matter serious.
Serious is what a government calls a problem it did not prevent. The people counted in this tally were not asked for their description.

variants.headline: The national mood, diminished
body: We are informed that national happiness now stands at {{happiness}} percent, some {{drop}} points below its former level and under the halfway mark. The figures are the state's own.

variants.headline: When the pot runs low
body: When the pot runs low, the square fills up.
